notes: Singlife Simple Term: entry age and medical-free renewal/conversion are not stated on the page or brochure (no product summary on file), so left out.

Singlife Elite Term II: term cell is the Regular Pay choice; Limited Pay covers to age 99 (page: "Coverage up to age 99"). Premium guarantee is not stated for the base plan (the "not guaranteed" footnote in the brochure attaches to the CI rider premium only). no_medical gives the conversion option only; the page also offers a Guaranteed Issuance Option to raise cover at key life events without medical check-ups (limited to 50% of the sum assured or S$500,000 per life, whichever is lower), but one quote cannot support both. Entry age not stated.

DIRECT term life: premium left out on purpose. The page says premiums stay the same throughout the premium payment period, but the brochure says a 5-year renewable term is re-priced by age at each renewal (maximum renewal age 80, cover to 85), and the DPI fact sheet says TPD pricing may change premiums. entry_age 19 to 65 is the page figure for DPI generally; the brochure says the exact limit depends on the coverage period. No health-check-free renewal/conversion is stated.

Singlife Comprehensive CI II: entry age and waiting period length are not stated (only "waiting period and survival period are applicable"). The plan also pays 20% extras for tumour surgery, ICU stay and 27 Special Benefit conditions.

Singlife Essential CI II: stages not stated as such (list of 14 illnesses plus 4 diabetic conditions); claims cell left out because CI payout is an early payout of the Death Benefit with a separate diabetic-conditions benefit and a 10% coronary procedure payout. Entry age and waiting period not stated.
Singlife Multipay CI II: waiting periods stated are between claims (1 year between CI claims, 2 years between recurrent claims), not after cover starts, so waiting is left out. Entry age not stated.

Singlife Health Plus: copay_cap and panel left out because the sources disagree. The brochure (accurate as at 26 August 2026) shows 5% capped at S$6,000 a policy year for treatment at A&E or preferred medical providers; the policy contract effective 1 April 2026 shows maximum S$3,000 a policy year in a cell that spans all four options. Resolve against the current product summary before showing a figure. The rider has Private and Public options (Prime/Lite) tied to Shield Plan 1 or Plan 2/3 respectively.

Singlife Health Plus Starter: no yearly co-payment cap stated for the rider; the preferred-provider condition is described on the Shield Starter plan, not the rider, so panel is left out. The Starter summary PDF file is named health-plus-product-summary.pdf and contains both the Shield Starter and Health Plus Starter summaries.
